claims.statement: The email reference applies across FPT, GHEC and GHES. The disposable-email reusable prohibits verification of temporary expiring-service addresses and points to noreply for commit privacy; privacy does not waive verification requirements.

The organization-domain reusable requires a verified address in the approved domain to receive that organization's email notifications where such a restriction exists. A verified unrelated address is insufficient; delivery is not enforcement assurance.

The unverified-address restrictions prohibit creating/forking repositories, creating issues/pull requests and commenting on issues, pull requests or commits. This explicit list must accompany DOCS-EMAILIDENTITY-3's broad statement that most actions are unaffected.

The same unqualified restriction list prohibits OAuth authorization, personal access token generation and email notifications for unverified addresses. Account linkage or IdP login alone does not establish these capabilities.

The list also prohibits starring repositories; creating/updating projects or gists; creating/using Actions; sponsoring developers; and accepting organization invitations. Product wildcard metadata does not independently verify every capability on every platform.

The managed-user section says accounts created after August 1, 2024 are unverified by default. This dated cohort qualifies the concept's general nonautomatic-verification prose and requires exact creation context, not universal inference about older accounts.

FPT/GHEC noreply format depends on account creation and privacy timing: after July 18, 2017 it includes numeric ID plus username; prior creation with privacy enabled before that date uses username-only format. The precise boundary and other combinations are not elaborated here.

The cloud procedure describes selecting or toggling the privacy setting to obtain ID-based noreply; username changes break old username-only attribution but not ID-based attribution. This is not evidence of preserved Verified signature status.
Linked commit-privacy and approved-domain procedures are unreviewed pointers in this receipt. No account state, address, token, notification setting or rights decision changes.
